export_controls.text:
This week, as a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, I heard from — and questioned — leading experts on how America can stay competitive and outpace China in the AI race.

Keeping our most advanced AI chips out of Chinese hands is crucial for both national security and economic strength. #HFAC  #CD6

deepseek.reason: The speaker says keeping the most advanced AI chips out of Chinese hands is crucial for national security and economic strength.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly endorses restricting advanced chip access to China.

export_controls.text: There have been delays in addressing emerging technologies, certainly including the fast moving areas of AI, quantum computing, synthetic biology. And as these global threats evolve, your Bureau must be able to compete in the private marketplace and other government agencies for the talent needed to keep up with these threats. In coming weeks, I plan to introduce the BIS Strength Act. It's legislation that'll prevent adversarial nations, certainly including China from acquiring a product that could boost their economic competitiveness in areas of concern, giving your Bureau the hiring authority to bring leading technologists in for 1-year terms at market competitive rates to craft smarter, faster policy.
export_controls.context: House hearing on the Bureau of Industry and Security FY 2026 budget, focusing on export controls and AI competition.

deepseek.reason: The speaker plans to introduce the BIS Strength Act to prevent adversarial nations from acquiring sensitive products and to strengthen BIS hiring.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The bill's purpose is described as blocking adversary acquisition, though details of the controls are not spelled out.
